Per stage: SST build 743 commits p99 0.2137 s (canonical synced write p99 0.0991 s, wallet synced write p99 0.0916 s, against 0.0014 s and 0.0002 s before the build); ingest stage 4 commits p99 0.0201 s; drop stage 931 commits p99 0.0251 s. subchecks.attribution: The excess is in the SST-build stage, not the IngestExternalFile call. Of 743 build-stage commits, 53 exceeded 2x the adjacent baseline p99 (0.0371 s): 18 were dominated by synced writes (up to 0.249 s), each within 40 s after this process did at least 1121 MB of IO in a 10-s sample; 35 fell in 04:19:51-04:20:26 UTC with wallet apply at a median 33 ms and no slower synced write (cause not isolated). The stage holds one canonical snapshot for the whole build, and the harness cannot separate that hold from the build's IO and CPU; Arm 1 holds of 30 s to 30 min alone show no excess. The spec defines Arm 2 as building the SSTs and ingesting while the writer commits, and the pre-registered criterion counts the whole attach phase, so this is counted as a trip of condition 2.

cancelled_controls.status: paired no-hold control at 60x did not complete: it ran 08:06:20-09:08:45 UTC, the shared host disk filled (free space fell from 24 GB at 08:06 to 0.14 GB at 09:08), the wallet stage detached with ENOSPC at t=3734 s, 63 s into the 15-minute post-release window, and the run exited 1; the release-equivalent point (09:06:32 UTC), the end of the natural window, and the forced-compaction point are after 09:00 or absent, and its first phase (08:06:32-08:36:32) overlapped 186 GB of other sessions' IO (no-reader commit p99 0.477 s against 0.037 s in the hold run's same phase), so none of its output is used

arm3_mainnet_extrapolation.label: Testnet measurement; the Mainnet figures are an extrapolation, not a measurement
arm3_mainnet_extrapolation.method: Scale total wall time linearly by the ratio of whole-chain transparent outpoint volume, measured as outpoint sorter bytes: Testnet 2,600,446,123 B at the rebuilt tip against about 99 GB for a late-2026 Mainnet build (docs/runbooks/initial-sync.md:129-130); the ratio is 19.0x to 38.1x depending on whether the 99 GB counts the merge's double footprint (density-derivation.json)
arm3_mainnet_extrapolation.mainnet_anchor: one measured Mainnet wallet construction from genesis took more than two hours (docs/runbooks/deploying-wallet-serving.md:327-329); the linear estimate sits above that, so treat it as an upper-leaning range
arm3_mainnet_extrapolation.rss: not extrapolated from chain size: the Testnet outpoint sorter fit in one run of 2.79 GB under this bench's 4 GiB outpoint budget (secondary sorters 1 GiB each); a Mainnet build fills the budget and spills, so peak RSS is set by the sorter budgets, not measured here
arm3_mainnet_extrapolation.staging: Testnet staging peaked at 6.06 GB; the runbook reports about 117 GB on Mainnet (docs/runbooks/initial-sync.md:136-138)
caveats: Mainnet's outpoint sorter needs several runs and a merge pass; Testnet needed one run and no merge, so merge IO is absent from the Testnet time

this bench sets a 64 GiB per-sorter spill ceiling (services/zinder-bench/src/rocksdb_wallet_rebuild.rs:26), below the about 99 GB a Mainnet outpoint sorter needs, so this exact configuration would stop on Mainnet

Arm 3 ran 01:58:48-02:09:51 UTC, before host-io.log started (02:21:46), so other sessions' IO during it is not recorded; load averages (1, 5, 15 min) were 2.75, 3.07, 2.71 at the start and 2.40, 3.40, 3.31 at the end (host-load.log)

not_shown: Mainnet behavior: every number is a Testnet replay of heights 4,580,001 to 4,596,483 or less; recent Testnet blocks average 11.9 KB and 1.7 transactions, and the density arms add synthetic ballast bytes, not real Mainnet rows

space return after a 30-minute hold under wallet-side churn: both paired no-hold controls were cancelled (60x died of a full disk 63 s into its post-release window; 10x was skipped), so condition 3 is not measured at density, and the 10x single-run result (20% returned in 15 minutes, 100% after forced compaction) is unresolved

the topology under test: canonical and wallet stay separate databases with separate synced batches, so one shared WriteBatch, one database-wide write controller, and canonical-to-wallet torn views are not exercised

absolute Mainnet commit latency: density ballast scales bytes written and compacted but not per-commit CPU (prepare, validation, readback, wallet derivation); canonical ballast keys are append-only, so hash-keyed canonical compaction debt is understated
real block spacing: only realtime-25s-hold-5m (72 commits, p99 equals max 0.0377 s) ran at 25-second spacing; every other number comes from 500 ms accelerated pacing

statistical depth: one run per arm, one repeat of hold-1s, n=1 per replacement shape, and a shared host where other sessions' IO reached 183 GB in one 30-minute phase; the host-quiet filter sees only processes it can read and treats zakurad as own load

a separation of Arm 2's causes: the SST build holds a canonical snapshot while sorting and writing, and the harness cannot apportion the slowdown between the hold and the IO; ingest into a fresh empty column family is the best case; catch-up copies delta rows from the live old family rather than deriving them
the design review's no-live-drop_cf amendment: Arm 2 tested live drop_cf (old files left disk 0.19 s after the last holder released), not DeleteRange truncation of a fixed family set
Mainnet rebuild cost: Arm 3 measured only Testnet; the Mainnet range is a linear extrapolation, and this bench's spill ceiling is too small for a Mainnet outpoint sorter
serving realism: Arm 4 is 24 in-process worker threads with zero think time, not the gRPC serving path, and wallet-family readers scan whole families
fault isolation: no crash, OOM, or reader-fault coupling between serving and the writer was tested

disk.note: work directories were hard-link copies of the input stores, so du at run end counts about 12.9 GB of shared input; all work directories and database copies are deleted; no new database copy or build artifact was made for this report
